title: Replayable implementation backbone
scope: A thin TypeScript/Node application core that stages and reviews synthetic evidence, persists append-only canonical history, projects deterministic Positions, reviews profile Claim revisions, and replays the same inputs.
non_goals: Graphology or other quantitative SNA Methods
LLM provider calls, AnalysisPort, branch search, or ForecastMatcher

criteria.expected: A pinned Node/TypeScript toolchain and lockfile can install and run the P1 tests without a global runtime dependency.
Persistence has explicit migrations/schema ownership for staging, evidence metadata, canonical Nodes/Relations/Flows/States/Events/Claims, revisions, and derived Positions.
Synthetic evidence enters staging, receives an explicit review decision, and only accepted material reaches canonical history.
Canonical writes are append-only, source evidence identity is retained, and a change journal identifies the writer and operation.
The Position projector deterministically reconstructs a question-bounded as-of Position from canonical rows, valid time, evidence cutoff, and profile snapshot identity.
The same evidence, projection identity, and cutoff reproduce the same Position; derived Position rows can be rebuilt without changing canonical history.
A reviewed time-bounded profile Claim revision appends a new revision, preserves the prior Claim and old profile snapshot, and affects only later projections.
Actual/reconstructed history and hypothetical/predicted records remain distinguishable at persistence and projection boundaries; P1 does not promote P0 Variations.
A synthetic P0 record can be imported, projected, revised, and replayed through the same application use cases used by future API clients.
P1 tests and the repository gate pass, with no private locator, case material, credential, or runtime artifact entering the public repository.
